why: Both moved the same two clients the same way, but B found and fixed a real translation defect — the leading SSE chunk carrying content "" instead of null — that silently turned every tool call into an empty text answer on exactly the path the app's users ride (astream_chat), while A's "verified end to end" run exercised the sync stream_chat path and so would likely have shipped that breakage. On system judgment B is also the one doing engineering rather than inference: its cache-key, fallback and declined-model-swap items are all priced and timed on live Router with the app's own prompts, including the key insight that the cache key must be conversation-scoped (and therefore cannot live in router.policy.json), whereas A's biggest cost lever (gpt-5-nano on analysis) is an unmeasured price-table argument.
A_best: The only genuinely complete end-to-end live run — one real question driving all 10 chained Router calls, 10/10 200 — plus feature labels that fix a measured feature=None on the streamed requests and make per-role policy addressable at all.
B_best: Catching the content ""-vs-null stream defect that killed the user-facing tool loop, isolated with a runtime-off control arm against a local stub, and the measured per-conversation prompt_cache_key (-25%/call) with the correct argument for why policy-level keying can't do it.
A_worst: Verification aimed at the wrong code path (sync stream_chat, not the astream_chat the websocket handler uses), so its 'behaviour unchanged, nothing loses' claim for the streaming agent is unsupported; i3 and i4, its main cost items, rest on list prices rather than any measurement.
B_worst: Weak spend attribution — only product=sec-insights, leaving feature as frame-derived names that A showed come out empty on the streamed path — plus a hand edit to the vendored runtime flagged by the check, tools.py:152 left unverified, and a probe script committed into backend/scripts.
